lines: On the Stride, the plan sets the belt speed and the incline.
Set up your run: HIIT intervals, or Steady, one speed and one incline held the whole run.
Minute on is six rounds: work at thirteen kilometres an hour on a two percent incline, recover at six.
Your run adds it up: sixteen minutes, about two point three five kilometres and thirty-five metres of climb.
Steady starts on Hill walk: six and a half, at eight percent.
Clip in the safety key and tap Start run.
Stand on the side rails: the belt starts in three.
Mid-run, speed reads nine kilometres an hour, six forty a kilometre, at target.
The trace draws speed against the plan, with the incline below.
Take over with Slower and Faster, a quick speed, or the incline bars.
Tap twelve. The belt ramps up, and the plan takes over again next interval.
On a phone, the controls follow the run.
What the tests prove: the belt starts only after a three, two, one countdown.
And if the Stride stays off for ninety seconds, the run ends.
That is journey six. Wattzup turns an Echelon bike or treadmill into a live training display.
